release_rule: No entry below 'reviewed' may be shown to a participant. Fill 'missing' with a first-language reviewer, then raise each status.
warning: Every consent-specific term is still missing. Nothing here may be shown to a participant until a first-language reviewer has filled the gaps and raised each status to 'reviewed'.
notes: The app's language list says 'Oshiwambo'. Oshiwambo is a cluster, and this source is specifically Oshindonga. Oshikwanyama differs in places, and the source says so itself. Decide with the lecturer whether the app offers 'Oshiwambo' as one option or splits Oshindonga and Oshikwanyama, because a participant will notice.
The guide is a Peace Corps-derived learner book. It is strong on greetings, health, the clinic and everyday words, and has nothing on consent, risk, confidentiality, ethics, witnesses or signatures.
'Read aloud = Lesha mokule' is the single most useful entry in this file: it is the instruction the field-capture screen gives the fieldworker.
Oshindonga is a Bantu language with noun classes; a single-word gloss changes shape inside a sentence.

t.yes.note: The guide notes that in reply to a negative question the answer is always ee-ee.

t.not_sure.note: Built from 'shi' = to know. Not a sourced phrase.

t.please.note: Oshindonga has no one-word 'please'. The guide's own advice is to use 'kwatha ndje' (help me), or 'alikana' when the request is urgent. A consent form must not sound like begging, so a reviewer should choose the register.

t.do_you_understand.note: Built from the attested 'Kandi uvite ko' = I don't understand, and 'uvite ko' = to understand. Confirm the question form.

t.when.note: 'Owa tameka okweehama uunake?' = when did you get sick?

t.age.note: 'Omvula' = year; age is counted in years. 'Owa za peni?' is given for 'how old are you', which a reviewer should check, since it literally asks where you are from.

t.sick.note: The guide gives 'Sick / In pain = Ehama' as the headword and explains ehama is the word for both.

t.where_hurt.note: Attested in the health section: 'What part of you is hurting?'

t.read_aloud.note: Directly attested: 'Read aloud = Lesha mokule'. This is the exact wording the capture flow needs. 'Popya mokule' = speak louder.

t.payment.note: From 'Futa' = to pay. 'Iimaliwa' = money. Noun form needs confirming.

t.not_paid.note: Built from 'Futa'. Not a sourced sentence.

t.study.note: The guide lists 'Study / Learn = ilonga / ilongo / ilonga' across tenses. This is 'to study' as a learner, not 'a research study'; a reviewer must supply the research sense.

t.language.note: Not in the extracted word lists. 'elaka' is standard. Confirm.

t.question.note: Not in the extracted word lists. Built from 'pula' = to ask. Confirm.

t.parent_guardian.note: Not sourced. 'Omukuluntu' = elder person is attested. The legal guardian concept needs a reviewer.
